{{recipesummary|category=Spanish recipes|servings=4|time=90 minutes|difficulty=1
| Image = [[Image:Fabes con almejas - Jlastras.jpg|350px]]
}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Spain|Cuisine of Spain]] | [[cookbook:Clam|Clam recipes]]

'''''Fabes con almejas''''', sometimes called ''habas con almejas'', (Spanish for beans with clams) is a clam and bean [[Cookbook:Stew|stew]] that originated in the principality of Asturias in Spain in the 1800s as peasant fare.<ref>[http://www.theheartofnewengland.com/food/shellfish/spanish-beans-clams.html ''Fabes con almejas'' recipe from the Heart of New England]</ref> It's a lighter variation of Asturian ''fabada'' whose primary ingredients are sausage, beans and pork.

The traditional recipe for ''fabes con almejas'' calls for small clams, white beans, onions, garlic, salt, saffron, bay leaves, olive oil, parsley, bread crumbs and sometimes sweet paprika.<ref>[http://www.spain.info/NO/TourSpain/Gastronomia/Productos%20y%20Recetas/Recetas/C/0/Fabes%20con%20almejas ''Fabes con Almejas'' recipe from Spain Info]</ref><ref>[http://www.freewebs.com/lokebuskes/cocina.htm ''Habas con almejas'' recipe from ''Lo Ke Busques'']</ref>

A small serving works well as an appetizer and a large serving is a satisfying main course.
==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] (450 g) dried white [[Cookbook:Beans|beans]] (e.g. navy, great northern, cannellini)
*24 live littleneck or mahogany [[Cookbook:Clam|clams]]
*3 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaves]]
*3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] extra-virgin [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (~ 4 oz) [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
*1 generous [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of [[Cookbook:Saffron|saffron]] or yellow [[Cookbook:Food Coloring|food coloring]]
*1 tablespoon sweet [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]] (not smoked)
*¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]
*A large loaf of crusty [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]]
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] as needed

==Procedure==
#Rinse the beans and [[Cookbook:Soaking Beans|soak]] overnight.
#Scrub the clams clean and rinse.
#Drain the beans and place them in a skillet with the onion, garlic, two pinches of parsley, bay leaves, and olive oil.
#Add just enough water to cover the ingredients and cook over a high flame.
#Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] and then reduce to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]]. Skim off any foam. Cook them, loosely covered, until done. This should take about 90 minutes. Check the skillet occasionally to add water. Never allow the water to drop below the height of the ingredients.
#When the beans are almost done, place the clams in a separate skillet and add about an [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] of water. Cover the skillet and cook over medium heat, shaking the pan occasionally to help the clams open. Check the clams every minute. Remove them as they open and place them in a separate bowl. This should take no more than 10 minutes. Once you've removed all the clams you'll have clam broth in the skillet. Save the broth, as you'll need it for the next step.
#Check the broth for bits of dirt and clam shell. If there's a lot, you'll have to strain it through a cloth to remove the grit.
#Add the broth to the simmering beans along with the saffron (or food coloring), the remaining parsley, paprika and salt to taste.
#Cover and cook for 5–10 minutes.
#Ladle the beans and broth into separate bowls and add six clams to each bowl.
#Serve with crusty bread on the side.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Be sure to follow the [[Cookbook:Clam|safe handling tips for clams]].

steps.text: Rinse the beans and soak overnight.
Scrub the clams clean and rinse.
Drain the beans and place them in a skillet with the onion, garlic, two pinches of parsley, bay leaves, and olive oil.
Add just enough water to cover the ingredients and cook over a high flame.

Bring to a boil and then reduce to a simmer. Skim off any foam. Cook them, loosely covered, until done. This should take about 90 minutes. Check the skillet occasionally to add water. Never allow the water to drop below the height of the ingredients.

When the beans are almost done, place the clams in a separate skillet and add about an inch of water. Cover the skillet and cook over medium heat, shaking the pan occasionally to help the clams open. Check the clams every minute. Remove them as they open and place them in a separate bowl. This should take no more than 10 minutes. Once you've removed all the clams you'll have clam broth in the skillet. Save the broth, as you'll need it for the next step.
Check the broth for bits of dirt and clam shell. If there's a lot, you'll have to strain it through a cloth to remove the grit.
Add the broth to the simmering beans along with the saffron (or food coloring), the remaining parsley, paprika and salt to taste.
Cover and cook for 5–10 minutes.
Ladle the beans and broth into separate bowls and add six clams to each bowl.
Serve with crusty bread on the side.
